fields.meta_title: Travel Reimbursement Form Priced by Per Diem | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a travel reimbursement form that prices meals at your per diem rate and checks each hotel night against a cap. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Travel Reimbursement Form That Prices Every Trip Day
fields.hero_description: Describe your meal rate and hotel cap. Emergent builds the travel reimbursement form, works out each day's allowance and saves every claim to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Blank Voucher Leaves to the Traveler
fields.features_subheading: A PDF has one line for meals and one for lodging. Everything between the rate table and the total is still the traveler's job.
fields.feature_1:
Meals priced from your rate table

Load GSA's per diem rates by city, or one flat company rate. Each claim fills the meal allowance for the destination and prices departure and return days at three-quarters of it.
fields.feature_2:
Served meals taken off the day

Ask which meals a conference or host provided on each day of the trip. The form subtracts that meal's share of the daily rate before the claim reaches anyone for approval.
fields.feature_3:
Hotel nights checked against a cap

Set a nightly lodging limit, flat or by city. A night above it splits into a covered amount and an overage, and the overage goes to whoever your policy names to approve it.
fields.feature_4:
Receipts required by amount

Ask for a receipt photo on every hotel bill and on any line at or above the amount you choose. Smaller lines need a note on their purpose. A claim missing an upload will not submit.
fields.feature_5:
A filing window on every claim

Count the days since each trip ended. Travelers get an email reminder a week before the window closes, and a late claim reaches finance marked with how many days past due it is.
fields.feature_6:
The claims app, exported to GitHub

Export the full codebase to your GitHub repository when finance wants the claims app on its own servers. Your rate table and every rule you prompted for travel with the code.

fields.usecase_heading: Claims From Four Kinds of Trips
fields.tab_content_1:
When the conference ends, the meals are priced

Professor Lena Ortiz spent three days at a conference in a city on the GSA standard rate. Calder State pays meals at that rate, $68 a day. She enters her travel dates, and the form allows $51 for each travel day. Her chair approves a $170.00 meal total, saved with the rate it used.
fields.tab_content_2:
Each night above $140 waits for the administrator

Pine Hollow County pays for hotels up to $140 a night. A health inspector back from a training files two nights at $172. The form covers $280.00 and holds the $64.00 overage with his note: the training hotel was the only one with rooms. Ruth Calloway, the county administrator, gets an email to decide it.
fields.tab_content_3:
With lunch served, $22 off each travel day

Board members at Fernhill Literacy travel in for a two-day retreat, and the nonprofit pays meals at $80 a day. Both are travel days, worth $60 each. The retreat served lunch on both, and the form takes $22 off each day. Joan Pruitt's claim comes to $76.00 for the treasurer.
fields.tab_content_4:
A claim held for one missing rental receipt

Halvorsen Engineering follows the IRS line on receipts: lodging always, and anything else at $75 or more. Priya Nair files a four-day site visit nine days after getting home. Her $412.00 hotel has a receipt, and the $38.00 taxi needs none. The $118.00 equipment rental does, and the $592.00 claim waits for it.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Travel Reimbursement Form
fields.howto_description: Start from the travel policy your finance team enforces, then turn each of its rules into a field or a check.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Get the travel policy in writing
fields.howto_step_1_des: Ask finance for the policy travelers are held to, even if it lives in an old email thread. Note the meal rate, the hotel cap, when receipts are required and how long travelers have to file. Each of those becomes a field or a check.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Load the daily meal rates you pay, whether GSA's published table or a single figure your company sets. Decide whether departure and return days pay three-quarters of the rate, as federal travelers get, or a full day. Put that rule in your prompt.
fields.howto_step_3_des: List the meals your daily rate covers and what each one is worth, such as $22 for lunch. The form needs those shares to subtract a meal that a conference or client paid for. Without them, travelers guess at the deduction.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Choose the amount at which a receipt becomes required. Many teams use the IRS line of $75, with lodging always included. A lower number means more uploads for finance to check, while a higher one means more lines accepted on the traveler's word.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write one prompt in plain English that covers each rule from your notes and names the approver. Emergent builds the travel reimbursement form, a claims table behind it and the approval step. Change a rule later by asking for the change in the same chat.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Point each claim at the traveler's manager, and send hotel overages to whoever your policy names. Add an email reminder before the filing window closes. Approved claims can sync to payroll or your accounting tool through its API.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it with a finished trip
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run one finished trip through the form, including a served lunch and a night over the cap. Compare its total with your own math. Then open the new row in the claims table and confirm that each field landed where finance expects it.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is blank claim vouchers posted by the organizations that pay them: a county PDF, a city day-trip form, UC Berkeley's domestic claim, a UMass spreadsheet, a member association's web form and two hosted copies on Jotform and Laserfiche. Each leaves the filer to look up the per diem, take a quarter off the travel days, subtract meals the event served and decide which receipts to attach. This page treats the travel reimbursement form as the after-trip claim priced against per diem: meals at the destination's daily rate with 75% travel days, provided meals deducted, hotels checked against a nightly cap, receipts asked for by the IRS line and a filing window. It answers the IRS and receipt questions searchers ask. Approval before the trip stays on the travel request sibling, general receipts on the expense report sibling and driving on the mileage sibling.
tab_stories: A Calder State professor files her three-day conference claim and the form prices meals at the $68 standard rate, paying $51 on each travel day, for $170.00 without her opening the GSA site.
Pine Hollow County caps hotels at $140 a night, so an inspector's two nights at $172 split into $280.00 the county pays and $64.00 that waits for the county administrator.
Fernhill Literacy pays board members $80 a day for meals, the retreat served lunch both days, so the form takes $22 off each $60 travel day and the claim comes to $76.00.

A Halvorsen Engineering field engineer files a four-day site visit nine days after returning; the hotel and a $118 equipment rental need receipts under the $75 line, the $38 taxi does not, and the $592.00 claim is blocked until the rental receipt is attached.

IRS Publication 463: receipts are needed for lodging and for any other expense of $75 or more
IRS Publication 463: under an accountable plan, expenses accounted for within 60 days and excess returned within 120 days are treated as a reasonable period
IRS Publication 463: you are traveling away from home when duties keep you away from your tax home substantially longer than an ordinary day and you need sleep or rest
IRS Publication 463: the standard meal allowance is prorated on partial travel days, 3/4 on the days you depart and return
